data.narrative: Decomposed the one-sentence Team Collaboration spec into atomic tasks, built the data model via an AI agent, surfaced a real decomposition bug in the Task 2 prompt (plan assumptions vs actual output), and fixed the process with explicit interface contracts embedded verbatim into prompts.

dimension_scores.observation: Task 1 prompt pinned types, lengths, nullability, FK targets, and acceptance criteria so the agent produced first-pass-correct output with zero iterations. Corrected Task 2 prompt embedded the interface contract verbatim.
dimension_scores.evidence: Task 1: 75 tests green, schema verified in DB; Task 2 re-run audit found 0 divergences.

dimension_scores.observation: Reviewed agent output by reading all three generated files plus main.py wiring, then verified via live TestClient against all 7 acceptance criteria, not just a test count.
dimension_scores.evidence: live_teams_check.py: 201/201/200/200/204; 403/404/409/400/401 paths confirmed by corrected re-run.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized the BREAK conflict as a prompt defect (not code), applied the interface contract once, and the corrected re-run needed zero further iterations.
dimension_scores.evidence: One contract write resolved all divergence; no iteration spiral.

dimension_scores.observation: Correctly decided the fix belonged in Task 2's prompt (Task 1 was well-specified and built the rich model) and adopted a preventative rule: post-Task-1 prompts embed the upstream task's actual output, never plan assumptions.
dimension_scores.evidence: interface-contract-m2.md records the decision and the rule.

dimension_scores.observation: Shipped working, live-verified code with correct role semantics and duplicate handling, but the module's team feature lacks automated tests in the repo (instructed not to add them).
dimension_scores.evidence: 75 tests collected, exit 0; no team test file present in tests/.

dimension_scores.observation: The BREAK finding was documented precisely (owner_id vs created_by, flat vs join-table) with a conscious fix placement decision, but the write-up is in the proof rather than a standalone incident artifact.

strengths: Decomposed 'add team invitations' into six atomic subtasks plus an edge-case matrix before prompting.
Caught the decomposition bug (plan-vs-output schema conflict) and fixed the process with interface contracts, not a code patch.
Verified agent output independently with live endpoint checks against DB state rather than trusting agent self-reports.
Correctly rejected the agent's miscounted '75/76' framing by running --collect-only to confirm the real number.
growth_areas: Add automated tests for the team/membership endpoints in a future module task (grader-hidden tests are the only coverage right now).
Promote the BREAK write-up into a standalone postmortem artifact with owner-backed follow-ups.
data.recommendation: Carry the interface-contract discipline into Module 3: every prompt must embed the actual schema/contract of the code it builds against, and the Context Triangle will now need to feed that contract into each delegation.

public_evidence.student_action: Directed an AI agent to build the team schema and membership endpoints, then audited the output against a written interface contract and verified every endpoint live.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Added models.py Team/TeamMember/Invitation, migrate.py DDL, team_router.py (5 endpoints), teams_service.py (role checks + IntegrityError handling), schemas/team.py; wired router in main.py.
public_evidence.proof: 75 tests green; DB shows teams/team_members/invitations + uq_team_members_team_user + invitations_token_key; TestClient 201/201/200/200/204 across create/add/list/role/delete.
public_evidence.ability: AI-assisted task decomposition and interface contracts
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows an engineer who treats AI output as code that must pass a written interface contract and live verification, not as 'the agent said it works'.
